name: Changpeng Zhao

summary.text: Changpeng Zhao, known as CZ, founded the cryptocurrency exchange Binance and ran it as chief executive until November 21, 2023, when he pleaded guilty in Seattle federal court to failing to maintain an effective anti-money-laundering program, agreed to a $50 million fine and resigned; Binance separately paid $4.3 billion. On April 30, 2024 Judge Richard Jones sentenced him to four months in prison, against a prosecution request for 36 months. On October 23, 2025 President Trump pardoned him. Zhao has said he has no business relationship with the Trump family or World Liberty Financial, whose USD1 stablecoin was used to settle MGX's $2 billion investment in Binance.

facts.claim: On November 21, 2023, Zhao pleaded guilty before a federal judge in Seattle to a single count of failing to maintain an effective anti-money-laundering program, a Bank Secrecy Act violation, agreed to pay a $50 million fine and stepped down as Binance's chief executive. He wrote that day: 'I made mistakes, and I must take responsibility.'
facts.quote: Zhao pleaded guilty to a single count of failing to maintain an anti-money-laundering program, and he stepped down as Binance's chief executive.

sources.title: Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao pleads guilty to federal charges, steps down
Binance's Canadian CEO steps down, pleads guilty to breaking anti-money laundering laws

facts.claim: On April 30, 2024, U.S. District Judge Richard Jones sentenced Zhao to four months in prison. Prosecutors had sought 36 months, the defence had asked for probation, and the guidelines range was 12 to 18 months; the judge said he was troubled by Zhao's decision to ignore U.S. banking requirements. Zhao was released in September 2024.
facts.quote: U.S. prosecutors had recommended a 36-month sentence for Zhao. The defense had asked for probation, and the sentencing guidelines called for a prison term of 12 to 18 months.

facts.claim: On October 23, 2025, the White House confirmed that President Trump had pardoned Zhao. Press secretary Karoline Leavitt said in a written statement that the president 'exercised his constitutional authority by issuing a pardon for Mr. Zhao, who was prosecuted by the Biden Administration in their war on cryptocurrency', and that the Justice Department and the White House Counsel's office had reviewed the request.
facts.quote: She said Trump had "exercised his constitutional authority by issuing a pardon for Mr. Zhao, who was prosecuted by the Biden Administration in their war on cryptocurrency."

facts.claim: Zhao posted on X on October 23, 2025: 'Deeply grateful for today's pardon and to President Trump for upholding America's commitment to fairness, innovation, and justice,' adding that he would 'do everything we can to help make America the Capital of Crypto and advance web3 worldwide.'
facts.quote: "Deeply grateful for today's pardon and to President Trump for upholding America's commitment to fairness, innovation, and justice."

facts.claim: Asked why he pardoned Zhao, President Trump said: 'I don't know, he was recommended by a lot of people,' and said he did not know Zhao and did not believe he had met him. In a November 2025 '60 Minutes' interview he said 'I don't know who he is' and, asked about Binance's role in the $2 billion USD1 transaction, 'I know nothing about it because I'm too busy.'
facts.quote: He said "I don't know, he was recommended by a lot of people."

facts.claim: In an interview with Fox News's Bret Baier, Zhao said his lawyers had submitted a pardon petition in April 2025, that the clemency was a 'surprise', and that he had never met the president; he denied business ties with Trump or his sons, calling the suggestion that he worked with a firm connected to Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr. 'categorically false'. Responding to Wall Street Journal reporting that his representatives sought a deal with World Liberty Financial after the 2024 election, he said: 'There's no deal, there has never been any discussions.'
facts.quote: Zhao rejected that account, saying "There's no deal, there has never been any discussions. It's as simple as that."

facts.claim: Zhao told CNBC in January 2026 that MGX chose USD1 for its investment in Binance: 'They choose USD1 ... My request to them was they pay us in crypto. I don't want to deal with banks, really,' and said his business relationship with the Trumps had been 'misconstrued'.
facts.quote: "They choose USD1," ... "My request to them was they pay us in crypto. I don't want to deal with banks, really."

facts.claim: Senator Elizabeth Warren called the pardon 'corruption'; Senate Banking Committee Democrats wrote to the Justice Department and Treasury on October 28, 2025 seeking information on it. These are allegations and requests, not findings.
facts.quote: On October 23, 2025, President Trump granted that pardon.

openQuestions: The pardon's signing date is reported variously as October 21 (Fox News citing DOJ), October 22 (journalists) and October 23 (White House confirmation; Senate letter). The justice.gov pardon list was not reached.
The Boston Globe 60 Minutes item's date and exact wording should be checked against the CBS transcript.
The Wall Street Journal's original report on Zhao's representatives and World Liberty Financial was not reachable.
